evidence.note: After the big implementation landed (jump from 2 to 376 passing), the agent immediately looped over multiple/all spec_json files to get per-file pass/fail counts and began categorizing failures (validation vs. real), establishing a concrete picture of what remained rather than assuming done.

Repeatedly re-ran the full per-file suite after each fix, tracking which families still had non-validation failures (memory 10, conversions 49, etc.) and reconciling counts as families went green — continuous per-family pass-count monitoring.

On moving to SIMD, enumerated exactly which SIMD families still failed and their counts (simd_const 5, simd_lane 8, simd_splat 8, all store_lane series), fixed each, and re-ran to confirm — a clear done/remaining picture at family granularity.

Computed the aggregate 32825/34212 = 0.9595 and quantified the concrete gap to 1.0 (the 1387 skipped assert_invalid/malformed assertions), knowing precisely what stood between current state and the bar.

The memory.json crash recurred across several iterations; the agent noticed it each cycle and pursued a new hypothesis (safer lookups, then capping memory allocation) rather than declaring victory, though it did not frame this as being 'stuck'.

reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate, continuously refreshed picture of per-family pass counts by re-running the whole suite after each fix and enumerating exactly which families remained (steps 56,64,75,84,87-91), and it quantified the concrete remaining gap to 1.0 (the 1387 skipped assertions at step 93) — clearly above the level-5 'keeps a checklist and generally knows what remains.' It falls short of level 8/10 because progress was re-derived by re-running tests rather than tracked in a persistent ledger, it never explicitly reconciled implementation against the full listed opcode surface (trusting test files as proxy), and there is no evidence it caught a fix in one family breaking another. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 7.
